videos.title: MANUAL GUIDE i Part 1 — Overview and Setup
topics_covered: Manual Guide i system overview and benefits
Soft keys, MDI panel, screen navigation
Overview of all turning cycles (drilling, turning, residual, grooving, threading)
Tool offset data: geometry offset, wear offset, tool data pages
Insert nose radius and virtual tip orientation (T-numbers 1-16)
Fixed forms: creation, import, deletion, customization (forms 1-5)
NC Guide offline software (3 versions: Academic, Standard, Pro)
G-code learning mode (cursor over code shows descriptions)

manual_guide_i_overview.description: Powerful onboard conversational programming system for Fanuc CNCs
capabilities: One screen to fully program a part
Import offline G-code programs for simulation
Mix G-code and conversational in one program
NC Convert: convert conversational to G-code
Time study: cut time + non-cut time breakdown
benefits: Ease of use — all cycles have similar fill-in-the-blanks interface
Flexibility — set up fixed forms your way
Learning tool — cursor over G/M codes shows descriptions
Mixed programming — G-code + conversational in one program
Simulation — both conversational and G-code programs

navigation.access_method: Graph function key or Custom function key on MDI panel
navigation.all_in_one_screen: Shows position, active program, active tool, feed rate, spindle speed, load meters
navigation.screen_shift: Left/Right arrow keys to navigate between screens

geometry_offset.radius: Insert nose radius (e.g., 0.031 for CNMG with #1 suffix)
geometry_offset.virtual_tip: Tool orientation number — CRITICAL for correct compensation

wear_offset.x_wear: Fine-tune X offset for tolerance control
wear_offset.z_wear: Fine-tune Z offset for tolerance control
wear_offset.radius: Auto-picks from geometry offset — only enter once

tool_data.tool_type: General, Threading, Grooving, Button, Straight, Drill, Chamfer, Flat End Mill, Ball Nose, Tab, Reamer, Boring Bar, Face Mill
tool_data.cut_angle: Lead angle of tool (e.g., 95° for 80° diamond, 93° for 35°/55° diamond)

virtual_tip_orientation.3: OD turning tool (top turret, most common)
virtual_tip_orientation.note: Same numbers used for bottom turret machines

fixed_forms.form_1: Start of program commands (tool change, start spindle, start lines)
fixed_forms.form_2: Cut speeds for different materials (mild steel, stainless, aluminum, cast iron, etc.)
fixed_forms.form_3: Drill cycles, tapping cycles, turning cycles, threading cycles
fixed_forms.form_4: Subprogram calls, G10 assign values, spindle start
fixed_forms.form_5: End of program (parts counter macro, M30, etc.)
fixed_forms.max_per_form: Up to 10 entries per form (or 5 if larger entries needed)
fixed_forms.import_export: Text file format (.dat), editable on PC, import via memory card
fixed_forms.settings_path: Edit → Right Shift ×4 → Settings → Register fixed form sentence

nc_guide_versions.standard: Full programming, can export programs to machines
nc_guide_versions.pro: Import machine ladder + parameters, full machine simulation

parameters.x_finish_amount: Stock per side for finish pass

detail_data.first_speed_override: % override for first pass only (for runout compensation)
detail_data.cut_rise_method: Always use 'cut rise' to avoid steps on shoulders
detail_data.approach_motion: Vector move, X then Z, or Z then X

in_face_machining.available: Yes/No — enables facing within turning cycle
in_face_machining.caution: Cannot use center — tool faces to X0

rules: Define FINISHED profile only — software calculates rough paths
Start at X0 Z0 (center of part face)
Arcs: CW or CCW + radius or center point
Corner radii: add between line/arc segments
Last element must be BLANK type (stock size)
Must close figure: Right shift ×4 → B continuous → Figure 1 (OD) or Figure 2 (ID)

program_a_b_sets.description: Multi-operation parts use A-set (first side) and B-set (flip part)
program_a_b_sets.program_stop: M00 with comment 'Turn part around' between sets

subprogram_creation.method: In geometry → Create → Insert sub-program (vs insert in current program)
subprogram_creation.result: Single M98 P-call line in main program

threading.finish_options: Finish stock amount OR number of finishing passes
threading.cut_type: Number of passes OR depth of cut
threading.thread_depth_calc: Press 'Calculate' soft key — auto-calculates from TPI
threading.left_hand_threads: Supported — multiple methods depending on tool orientation
threading.thread_taper: General thread type supports any angle
threading.thread_repair: Available but requires builder ladder development

nc_convert.access: Auto mode → Right Shift → NC Convert soft key
nc_convert.process: Reads conversational program → generates point-to-point G-code
nc_convert.output: Standard G-code — portable to any Fanuc control without Manual Guide i

time_study.access: Sim Lab → Right Shift → Insert Time
time_study.note: Non-cut time requires real machine feedback for accuracy

fixed_form_import.path: Edit → Right Shift ×4 → Settings → Register fixed form sentence for milling
fixed_form_import.caution: NEVER press Standard button — deletes all fixed forms

tool_data_import.note: Only requires single confirmation (unlike fixed forms)

milling_blank_definition.centering: Set work origin X/Y to half-dimensions for center = X0 Y0

drilling.go_past_amount: Extra depth for drill point angle
drilling.detail_data: Optional: slow start feed until fully engaged, slow down at bottom

rectangle_pattern.skip_holes: Optional — maintain pattern but skip selected positions

point_patterns.copy_paste: Point patterns can be copied and pasted to reuse across cycles

parameters.side_stock: Optional — asterisk (solid part assumed if blank)
parameters.cut_depth_of_axes: Z depth of cut per pass
parameters.finish_stock: Leave stock for finish pass (0 = machine to size)

gcode_conversion_output.contour: Point-to-point moves (no G41/G42 unless parameter enabled)

simulation_features.3d_rotation: Rotate view to see from any angle
simulation_features.cut_display: Cut away portion of blank to see internal features
simulation_features.tool_display: Requires D-word in program + tool data radius defined

thread_milling.overlap_parameter: 27451 (number of insert teeth for overlap calculation)
thread_milling.tool_type: Use TAP type in tool data (no dedicated thread mill type)

types.type_1: Single revolution — thread mill with multiple flutes (like a tap shape)
types.type_2: Thread revolution — single point tool, one revolution per pitch
types.type_3: Multi-tip insert — multiple cutting tips, auto-calculates revolutions

thread_milling.point_patterns: Same as hole machining — random, linear, grid, rectangle, circle

thread_repair.description: Pick up existing thread on part, extend, repair deformities, re-chase
thread_repair.requirements: Builder must develop ladder logic — Fanuc standard ladder insufficient
procedure: 1. MDI: make threading tool active, set work offset at part face
2. Jog/Handwheel: move tool to thread, center insert in thread groove
5. Fill 6 tabs: Orient → Cut conditions → Detail → Position → Thread data → Execute
6. Press Measure to sync Z-axis with spindle C-axis
7. Move tool out of thread → OT Off → Start
thread_repair.orient_trick: Hold white business card behind thread for contrast when aligning
thread_repair.g76_compatibility: Can orient with Manual Guide i, then run standard G76 cycle

tool_types: Drill (small center drill recommended — HSS more forgiving)

limitations.single_font: Cannot change font — one built-in font only

embossing.description: Define rough stock outline so tool only removes material where stock exists
embossing.benefit: Eliminates air passes when milling non-rectangular features from rectangular stock

programming_languages.language_a: Both bits 0 — uses G50 for RPM limit (CSS)
programming_languages.language_c: Bit 7 = 1 — uses G92 for RPM limit
programming_languages.determination: G50 RPM limit = Language A, G92 RPM limit = Language C

fine_tuning_parameters.tool_data_access: Highlight T-line → press Input → jumps to tool offset table

frequently_asked_questions.access_manual_guide: Graph key, Custom 1, Custom 2, or dedicated MGI hard key (90% are Graph or Custom)
frequently_asked_questions.change_blank_size: Start → Blank tab → select type → fill fields → Insert
frequently_asked_questions.import_fixed_forms: Edit → Right Shift ×4 → Settings → Register → Input from memory card
frequently_asked_questions.change_fixed_form: Arrow to entry → Alter → edit → Alter
frequently_asked_questions.tool_not_showing: Need D-word in program + radius in geometry offset + correct tool type
frequently_asked_questions.create_new_tool: Go to empty tool offset → enter radius → set tool type
frequently_asked_questions.tool_offsets_shared: Yes — data entered in Manual Guide i is used on G-code side too
frequently_asked_questions.simulate_gcode: Yes — import G-code program and simulate in Manual Guide i
frequently_asked_questions.undo_button: Available in Edit mode — appears after accidental delete
frequently_asked_questions.material_table: NOT available — use fixed forms for material-specific speeds/feeds

mirror_image.method_1: Fixed form with G51.1 and axis specification
mirror_image.method_2: Mirror option within free-form geometry drawing
mirror_image.use_case: Mirror pocket or feature from one side of part to other

cutter_compensation.default: Manual Guide i does NOT output G41/G42 — uses tool diameter internally
cutter_compensation.conversational_mode: Changing tool size regenerates code automatically
cutter_compensation.converted_gcode: Uses original tool size — no G41/G42 unless parameter enabled

prerequisites.manuals: Fanuc manual S7 version (latest) or earlier version — step-by-step setup guide
prerequisites.ladder_logic: Builder must develop ladder for manual probing functions

prerequisites.probe_activation: Builder-specific M-code to turn on spindle probe — MUST activate before probing

fields.height_of_plane_reference: Face of spindle position relative to machine zero — CRITICAL (often = parameter 19702 for 5-axis)

probe_length.method: Z-axis approach to known surface, double touch

stylus_ball_diameter.method: Measure 4 sides of known-diameter ring gauge or bore
stylus_ball_diameter.requirements: Known diameter reference (ring gauge, precision bore)
stylus_ball_diameter.tips: Use good surface finish, round reference for best accuracy

touch_sensor.description: Table-mounted tool setter (Renishaw TS27R, Blum, etc.)

manual_probing_tabs.tab_1_calibration: Probe length, stylus diameter, stylus offset, touch sensor

tab_2_tool_measurement.method: Double touch — always measures twice for accuracy

types.single_surface_z: Touch top of part → set Z work offset
types.single_surface_x: Touch side of part → set X work offset
types.outside_diameter: Touch 2 or 4 sides → find center (eliminates manual calculation)
types.inside_diameter: Touch 4 sides of bore → find center
types.c_axis_outside: Measure on C-axis (can change to B or A axis)

tab_3_work_set.workflow: Fill parameters → press Measure → press Set → dumps value to work offset
tab_3_work_set.work_offsets: G54-G59 + G54.1 P1-P48 = 62 total work offsets
tab_3_work_set.flexibility: Set value to 0, positive, or any value — adapts to programming style

tab_4_measure.use_case: In-process quality checking — set tolerance range for pass/fail
tab_4_measure.tolerance_range: OK range parameter — alarm if out of spec

automatic_cnc_probing.access: Edit mode → Right Shift → MCyc soft key
automatic_cnc_probing.difference_from_manual: Inserts G-code cycle into program — runs automatically
automatic_cnc_probing.output: 4-digit G-code that runs on any Fanuc control with Manual Guide i
automatic_cnc_probing.additional_parameters: More fields than manual (approach positions, feed rates, clearances)
automatic_cnc_probing.can_import_to: CAM-generated G-code programs — insert probing cycles anywhere
automatic_cnc_probing.calibration_cycles: Probe length + stylus diameter (auto version needs XY approach position + feed rates)

vs_renishaw.fanuc_probing: Built-in P-code macro programs — NOT Renishaw 9000 series
vs_renishaw.renishaw_compatible: Can download Renishaw cycles into fixed forms and insert into programs

quality_checking.ok_range: Set tolerance band — alarm if measurement outside range
quality_checking.use_case: High-volume production — check bore/feature every N parts

videos.title: AIT220 Lecture 10 — FANUC Macros and Miscellaneous Commands
topics_covered: Macro vs ordinary teach pendant programs (Fanuc Robotics context)
Program subtype: None vs Macro declaration
Macro assignment to user keys (Tool 1-7, Shift+Tool 1-7)
Quick menus vs full menus (operator lockout)
Robot input and UI/PLC input triggers

key_knowledge.note: This video covers Fanuc ROBOTICS macro programming, not CNC macros. The concepts of variables, registers, branching (CALL, LABEL, GOTO), and macro configuration are transferable but the specific implementation differs from CNC custom macros. Key CNC macro concepts documented in the fanuc_reference section below are derived from standard Fanuc CNC documentation rather than this robotics lecture.

macro_definition.description: An ordinary teach pendant program declared with subtype=Macro
macro_definition.declaration: Program Detail screen → Subtype → change from None to Macro
macro_definition.auto_declaration: Assigning program in macro configuration auto-sets subtype to Macro

group_mask.description: Controls whether program is allowed to move axes
group_mask.star: Not allowed to move any axes in group — data manipulation only
group_mask.one: Allowed to move axes in group — requires shift key on user buttons
group_mask.impact: Programs with group mask=1 require Shift+key, mask=* can run directly

manual_function_screen.configuration: Setup → Macro → define program name + assign to MF slot
manual_function_screen.benefit: Longer descriptive names vs 8-char program names

user_key_assignment.shift_keys: Shift + any of 7 keys for motion-allowed macros
user_key_assignment.requirement: Teach pendant must be ON for user key macros to execute

group_mask_impact.star: Can assign to direct key press (no shift needed)
group_mask_impact.one: Must use Shift+key (SU assignment) because axes may move

digital_input_trigger.description: Sensor input triggers macro execution automatically
digital_input_trigger.use_case: Part detection on conveyor, counting, automated response
digital_input_trigger.configuration: Setup → Macro → choice → Digital Input → specify DI number
digital_input_trigger.behavior: Macro executes completely when input goes TRUE

quick_menus.password: 4-digit passcode to return to full menus
quick_menus.purpose: Prevent operators from accessing setup/configuration screens

miscellaneous_instructions.message: Send text to User screen for logging/notification
miscellaneous_instructions.registers: Add, subtract, multiply, divide on data registers

fanuc_reference.description: Consolidated reference of all G-codes, M-codes, macro variables, canned cycles, and controller features documented across all 6 videos plus standard Fanuc CNC knowledge

tool_compensation.G41: Cutter compensation left (tool left of path)
tool_compensation.G42: Cutter compensation right (tool right of path)

turning_canned_cycles.G70: Finish turning canned cycle (follows G71/G72 rough profile)
turning_canned_cycles.G72: Multi-pass rough facing cycle (or rough grooving)

milling_canned_cycles.G82: Counter boring / spot drilling with dwell
milling_canned_cycles.G83: Peck drilling cycle (full retract between pecks)
milling_canned_cycles.G86: Boring cycle (feed in, spindle stop, rapid out)
milling_canned_cycles.G89: Boring cycle (feed in, dwell, feed out)

threading.G76: Multi-pass threading cycle (auto infeed, auto depth calculation)
threading.G92: Threading cycle (simple, single-pass definition) — also RPM limit in Language C

turning_specific.G50: Max spindle speed limiter (Programming Language A)
turning_specific.G92_rpm: Max spindle speed limiter (Programming Language C)

probing.G31: Skip signal (touch probe trigger — rapid stop on signal)
probing.note: Manual Guide i probing uses P-code macros, not direct G31 calls

special.G10: Data setting by program (assign values to offsets/parameters)
special.G51.1: Mirror image ON (specify axes to mirror)

manual_guide_i_internal.note: 4-digit G-codes are Manual Guide i internal — auto-generated

m_codes.M00: Program stop (operator must press cycle start to continue)
m_codes.M01: Optional stop (stops only if optional stop switch is ON)
m_codes.note: Probe activation M-code is builder-specific (varies by machine)

t_codes_and_offsets.format_turning: T0101 — first 2 digits = tool position, last 2 = offset number
t_codes_and_offsets.format_milling: T-number selects tool, H-word selects length offset, D-word selects radius/diameter offset
t_codes_and_offsets.h_word: Tool length compensation number (used with G43)
t_codes_and_offsets.d_word: Diameter/radius compensation number (used with G41/G42, also triggers simulation display)

offset_types.geometry: Base tool dimensions (length, radius, nose radius, virtual tip)
offset_types.wear: Fine-tune adjustments for tolerance control (added to geometry)

macro_programming.note: CNC custom macro B standard — the robotics lecture covers conceptually similar but different implementation

variables.local: #1-#33 — arguments passed via G65 call (A=#1, B=#2, C=#3, etc.)
variables.common: #100-#199 — common variables (volatile, lost at power off on some controls)
variables.permanent: #500-#999 — permanent common variables (retained at power off)
variables.system: #1000+ — system variables (current position, offsets, parameters, etc.)

calling.G65: Macro call — G65 P<program> A<arg> B<arg> C<arg>...

arithmetic.manual_guide_calculator: Control+W activates calculator in any Manual Guide i field — supports all math functions

p_code_macros.description: Probing cycles use P-code macro variable areas
p_code_macros.parameters: 12381-12388 define macro variable areas for probing
p_code_macros.execution: Button press triggers jump to stored macro number

controller_models_mentioned.series_31i: Confirmed compatible with Manual Guide i
controller_models_mentioned.note: Manual Guide i available on all current Fanuc CNC series

key_parameters.12381_to_12388: P-code macro variable areas for probing
key_parameters.27451: Thread milling overlap (number of insert teeth)

constant_surface_speed.g96: CSS ON — control adjusts RPM as diameter changes
constant_surface_speed.rpm_limit: G50 S-value (Language A) or G92 S-value (Language C)
constant_surface_speed.example: G96 S600 with G50 S1500 = 600 SFM max 1500 RPM

turning_depth_of_cut.finish_stock: 0.010-0.015 inch per side X, 0.005 inch Z (shoulders)

milling_step_over.pocket_mill: Typically half cutter diameter for roughing
milling_step_over.contour: Full width of cut with arc approach

simulation_capabilities.turning: 2D cross-section with tool path + material removal
simulation_capabilities.milling: 3D solid with material removal, rotation, zoom, cross-section
features: Simulates both conversational AND imported G-code programs

nc_convert.description: Convert conversational program to standard G-code
nc_convert.portability: Output runs on any Fanuc control without Manual Guide i

tips_and_best_practices: Always define blank at program start — simulation defaults to last blank used
Always include feed rate in start lines — prevents 'no feed rate' alarm even though cycles set feed
Use Input key to enter field values, Insert soft key only when ALL fields complete
Always set tool data correctly before programming — wrong data = wrong compensation = scrap
Simulate each cycle immediately after creation — catch errors early
Copy/paste geometry profiles between rough and finish cycles — avoid re-drawing
For turning profiles: define FINISHED shape only — software calculates rough passes
Last geometry element must be BLANK type (stock diameter) for turning profiles
Close all turning figures: Right shift ×4 → B continuous → select Figure 1 (OD) or 2 (ID)
Use G10 or fixed forms for material-specific speed/feed presets (no built-in material database)
D-word must be in program for tool to display in simulation
Calibrate probe before any probing operations — saves hours of troubleshooting
Activate probe M-code (builder-specific) before ANY probing — damage results otherwise
Thread repair requires builder ladder development — standard ladder insufficient
For engraving, use small HSS center drill — more forgiving than carbide
G50.1/G51.1 for mirror image — useful for symmetric features
Control+W in any Manual Guide i field activates built-in calculator
Background editing possible while machine runs — but NOT recommended for safety
Probing always measures twice for accuracy (parameter can disable second touch)
NC Guide offline software has 3 versions (Academic/Standard/Pro) — excellent for training
